{
  "$description": "RAMP RECIPE — the input to tier 1. Every primitive ramp step is COMPUTED from this file by ramps.mjs; none is hand-picked. A family is one seed hex: its OKLCH hue and its saturation (as a fraction of the chroma sRGB can actually render at that hue) are carried across a shared lightness ladder. That is what makes a rebrand one hex instead of eleven, and what makes `600` mean the same thing in every family.",
  "ladder": {
    "0": 1,
    "50": 0.983,
    "100": 0.96,
    "200": 0.916,
    "300": 0.85,
    "400": 0.741,
    "500": 0.632,
    "600": 0.534,
    "700": 0.436,
    "800": 0.338,
    "900": 0.241,
    "950": 0.145,
    "$description": "Shared OKLab lightness per step — the same in every family, which is the whole point. The step SIZES are not uniform, and shouldn't be: 50/100/200 are grounds, and a ground's job is to sit near paper, so the ladder is dense there (ΔL 0.017–0.044), opens through the middle (~0.109), and holds ~0.098 from 500 down. That last stretch is not a choice — it is fixed at both ends by the contrast anchors below and by the ink pin at 950. An earlier revision spread the steps evenly instead, which is defensible on paper and wrong in the room: it dragged neutral.100 from #F5F5F5 to #EDEDED and neutral.200 to #DBDBDB, and every ground, border and muted chip in the system picked up grey. Three steps are anchored so a cross-family rule can exist: 500 ≥ 3:1 (borders, large text, UI boundaries), 600 ≥ 4.5:1 (body text), 700 ≥ 7:1 (AAA). Two things about those anchors are deliberate. (a) They are measured against `background` — neutral.50, the ground the system actually paints on — not against #FFFFFF. Anchoring to white overstates every ratio by ~7%, which is enough to put a step on the wrong side of 4.5. (b) They are set against the WORST family, not the average: chroma contributes to WCAG luminance and OKLab L does not know that, so green rides ~0.15 higher in contrast terms at the same L. Anchoring to the average ships a rule that quietly fails for one hue — the exact failure this ladder exists to end. Deeper grounds (muted at neutral.100) are NOT covered by the ladder; those pairings are the contrast gate's job, and they are why muted-foreground sits a step below text-tertiary. 950 is pinned to the ink #0A0A0A — the neutral ramp is tints of one ink, and that ink is identity. THAT PIN IS A PROPERTY OF THIS LADDER, not of the system: presets.json now also holds ladders whose paper is off-white and whose ink stops short of 0.145, because pinning both ends in every preset is what froze `surface`, `card` and `foreground` to one value each across 60 rolls. Within any ladder the relationship still holds — paper is the lightest step, ink the darkest, monotonic in between — and this one is the ladder the checked-in system is."
  },
  "tint": {
    "$description": "THE NEUTRAL TINT — the hue and the small absolute chroma the achromatic family carries, so the greys can be warm or cool rather than dead. Before this existed `buildFamily` wrote C = 0 for the neutral family unconditionally, which made warm-versus-cool grey — arguably the loudest single decision in a real system — unreachable at any setting. Held here rather than derived from the neutral seed on purpose: the seed is DISCARDED (parity.test.mjs swaps it for magenta and asserts identical output), and reading a hue off it would turn a deliberately dead input back into a live one and put two controls on screen for one number. `chroma` is absolute and flat across the ramp; ramps.mjs tapers it only where the sRGB gamut physically runs out, which at L = 1.0 is everywhere — so a tint is only visible on `surface`/`card` under a ladder whose paper comes off 1.0. `{ hue: 0, chroma: 0 }` is the checked-in system and is what `presets.json`'s `tints.neutral` restates; test/expand.test.mjs compares them so the duplication cannot drift.",
    "hue": 0,
    "chroma": 0
  },
  "envelope": {
    "0": 0,
    "50": 0.018,
    "100": 0.038,
    "200": 0.072,
    "300": 0.112,
    "400": 0.15,
    "500": 0.185,
    "600": 0.168,
    "700": 0.14,
    "800": 0.11,
    "900": 0.08,
    "950": 0.058,
    "$description": "Shared ABSOLUTE chroma ceiling per step. Without it, a family whose hue has a wide gamut at high lightness (green, yellow) would render its 50/100 as saturated mint or cream while blue's stayed a whisper — the failure the hand-authored ramps avoided by eye and could not state. The ceiling is what makes every family's 50 the same strength of wash. Mid-ramp it is generous enough that most families are limited by their own gamut instead, which is correct: that limit is real."
  },

The seed IS the brand hex of record; the rendered 600 step sits a hair darker because the ladder's 600 is anchored to 4.5:1 for the WORST family (green), and moving it to match this hue exactly would drop moss-600 below AA.",
